headline: Canada's Southernmost Mainland Point Access
reservation: Point Pelee does not currently require a timed entry reservation for general park admission, though fees apply at the gate. During the Festival of Birds in May, specialized morning programs may require separate booking. Accommodation within the park is limited to oTENTik units which require advance reservation through the Parks Canada booking system; verify all seasonal hours on the official site.

days.title: The Southern Tip and Coastal Sands

stops.name: The Tip
stops.detail: Stand at the southernmost point of mainland Canada where Lake Huron currents meet.

stops.name: West Beach
stops.detail: Walk the sandy shoreline and observe the varied birdlife along the western coast.

days.driving: Allow 20–30 minutes; park shuttle runs from the Visitor Centre to the Tip.
days.note: Walking to the Tip is an option, but the seasonal shuttle saves significant time.

days.title: Marshlands and Migratory Pathways
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM from the Visitor Centre

stops.name: Marsh Boardwalk
stops.detail: Traverse the floating boardwalk to view the freshwater marsh ecosystem and observation tower.

stops.name: DeLaurier Homestead
stops.detail: Explore the history of early settlers and the evolution of the park's landscape.

days.driving: Allow 10–20 minutes; roads are well-maintained and easy to navigate.
days.note: Binoculars are highly recommended for the marsh tower to spot migratory species.

days.title: Carolynian Forest and Quiet Trails
days.start: Suggested: 8:30 AM from the North Gate

stops.name: Woodland Nature Trail
stops.detail: Meander through one of the most biodiverse forest regions in the country.

stops.name: Tilden Woods
stops.detail: Seek out unique flora and elusive songbirds in this sheltered interior woodland.

days.driving: Allow 15–25 minutes; easy access to trailheads from the main park road.
days.note: Insect repellent is often necessary when exploring the interior forest trails.

intel.title: Visitor Centre Hub
intel.text: Primary parking is located at the Visitor Centre, where the shuttle departs for the Tip. Secondary lots at the Marsh Boardwalk fill quickly during peak migration seasons.

intel.title: International Roaming
intel.text: Due to the proximity to the United States, phones may connect to American towers. Check your mobile plan for roaming charges while near the shoreline.

intel.title: Leamington Services
intel.text: The town of Leamington provides all necessary fuel and grocery services just minutes from the park gate. No fuel is available within the national park boundaries.

intel.title: Bird Migration Peaks
intel.text: May is the busiest month for birdwatching; expect heavy crowds and consider arriving at opening time. Late September offers a quieter experience for Monarch butterfly migration.

intel.title: Shuttle Service
intel.text: The Tip shuttle operates seasonally to reduce traffic on the narrow southern peninsula. Check the Visitor Centre for the daily schedule and last return times.

plan.arrival: Arrive at Windsor International (YQG) and drive southeast; Leamington is the primary gateway for lodging and last-minute supplies.
plan.vehicle: Small to mid-size cars are best suited for the park's narrow loop roads; larger RVs may find the Marsh Boardwalk parking restrictive.
plan.goldenHour: The Tip observation area is ideal for viewing the sunrise over the lake during the spring and autumn months.
